summary.one_liner: Devika is an experimental open-source AI software engineer that takes high-level coding objectives, breaks them into steps, researches them via web browsing, and writes code, positioned as an alternative to Cognition's Devin.
summary.what_it_does: Devika accepts natural-language task descriptions through a chat interface and plans them into steps using LLMs and reasoning algorithms. It can run web searches (Bing or Google search APIs) and browse pages with Playwright to gather information, and it writes code in multiple languages. It tracks agent state visually and organizes work into projects. The README lists support for Claude 3, GPT-4, Gemini, Mistral, Groq, and local models via Ollama, and it mentions a Netlify API key setting for deploying web projects. The README describes the project as in a very early, experimental stage with many unimplemented or broken features. A note at the top says a second iteration, Opcode, is coming soon.
use_cases: prototyping a software project from scratch
fixing bugs with an AI pair programmer
running local LLMs for coding agents
how_to_run: Clone the devika repository and cd into it
uv venv, activate it, then uv pip install -r requirements.txt
python devika.py to start the server
In a second terminal: cd ui/, bun install, bun run start
Open the web interface in a browser and configure API keys on the settings page
stack: Claude 3, GPT-4, Gemini, Mistral, Groq APIs
notable: Modeled after Devin by Cognition AI, aiming to be an open-source alternative
Supports many LLM providers plus local models through Ollama
Browser-based research via Playwright and Bing or Google search APIs
Config file created on first run and edited through the UI settings page
caveats: README says the project is in a very early, experimental stage with many unimplemented or broken features
Requires several API keys for search and LLM providers for full functionality
Requires Python 3.10+, uv, bun, and Playwright browser installs
